follow-up time: From birth to diagnosis of primary ciliary dyskinesia
cohort: Neonates born after 1994: 46 with primary ciliary dyskinesia and 46 controls with respiratory distress requiring a chest radiograph
finding: Term neonates with primary ciliary dyskinesia were more likely to require oxygen therapy, have a longer duration of oxygen therapy, have a later onset of neonatal respiratory distress, and have a higher frequency of lobar collapse and situs inversus.
